 now 11.35 EST GOAL! Arsenal 1-0 Hull CIty (Odegaard 72)
 Premier League: Arsenal finally break the deadlock at the Emirates, where Martin Odegaard has dinked the ball over Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who had just palmed away a shot by Noni Madueke.
 Share 3m ago 11.32 EST FA Cup: Barnsley have hit Aldershot for six and Cameron McGeehan has just scored his hat-trick at Oakwell.
 Share 4m ago 11.30 EST Championship: It’s Blackburn 2-0 West Ham at Ewood Park, where Oladapo Afolayan has fired a low shot home from just outside the penalty area. Meanwhile at St Andrews, 10-man Swansea Cirty have equalised against Birmingham City through a Christopher Klarer own goal at a corner.

Declan Rice has just been subbed off by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. The midfielder and Kai Havertz have been replaced by Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino.

 Thierno Barry double fires Everton to comeback win against Coventry Read more View image in fullscreen Thierno Barry scored his fifth and sixth goals of the Premier League season as Everton beat Coventry City last night. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA Share 3h ago 08.55 EST FA Cup first round
 In yesterday’s Football Daily email , John Brewin previewed his pick of the weekend’s first round games featuring the return of his beloved Macc, a 40-year-old cult hero lining up for the lowest ranked team in the competition and the club that purports to be the oldest in London. Read on …
 For the FA Cup , the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid …
 Mansfield v Macclesfield 
 In January, Macclesfield achieved the greatest shock in the competition’s history, knocking out the holders, Crystal Palace, in the third round. John Rooney’s National League North team head through the Pennines to face soundalikes Mansfield. Those from Macclesfield often find themselves having to correct others on coming from the Cheshire town rather than the one in Nottinghamshire. Macclesfield are such a modern club these days they have a sporting director in Keith Curle, a former Stags manager. Curle and current Mansfield boss Nigel Clough were England teammates at Euro 92, of which the less said the better .
 Bradford City v Marine
 Merseyside’s most authentic, proper football club? Neither Everton nor Liverpool can compete with Crosby’s Marine. When modern football gets too much, the temptation to savour a pie and pint at Rossett Park, the club of Roly Howard, legendary manager for 33 years, becomes strong. On Saturday, Marine travel to Bradford City, on something of a slide since Graham Alexander de-camped to manage Preston.
 Burton v AFC Rushden & Diamonds
 Fans at Burton’s Pirelli Stadium will see Billy Sharp’s comeback at 76. One of the Football League’s very top marksmen, the Championship’s all-time scorer on 130 recently retired but has returned with AFC Rushden & Diamonds, the phoenix club of a former temporary employer for whom he scored his first goal when loaned there in 2005, before they were liquidated six years later. A striker who defines the term “well-travelled” – including a spell at LA Galaxy – blink and you will miss Sharp, as the prodigal return is for one game only, in search of his 300th career goal. He departed Doncaster on the tantalising total of 299.
 Plymouth Argyle v Alvechurch 
 Alvechurch, representing a Worcestershire village, was previously most famous for giving the world Alan “Smudger” Smith (incidentally another member of that Euro 92 squad). The less said about his substitution for old pal Gary Lineker against Sweden the better. Smith’s alma mater, in the Southern League, travel to Plymouth Argyle, led by Tom Cleverley, the former brand turned aspirant tracksuit manager. Two seasons ago the Pilgrims’ progress down to League One was offset by beating eventual Premier League champions Liverpool in the third round. Should that fall flat, the city gets another helping on Monday night when Parkway take on Berkhamsted, the commuter town’s community club.
 Cray Wanderers v Stockport County 
 Representing the Isthmian League are Cray Wanderers, who claim to be London’s oldest football club, whose origins are traced to 1860, older perhaps than even Notts County. Playing in Chislehurst, best known for its caves, “The Wands” take on high-flying League One Stockport County, led by The Wire’s Jimmy McNulty.
 Peterborough v Reading
 All that and a Savage family reunion as the Posh, managed by Robbie, host son Charlie’s team, the Royals. The Cup properly runneth over.

 There are just the two top flight three o’clock kick-offs this afternoon, with Arsenal hosting Hull City at the Emirates and Fulham welcoming Newcastle United to Craven Cottage for an afternoon beside the Thames.
 Beyond the top flight, there’s plenty of Championship action to keep us entertained, while there are no fewer than 33 FA Cup first round matches slated for today. The phoenix club AFC Rushden & Diamonds from the Northern Premier League Division One Midlands (English football’s eighth tier) are the lowest ranked side in action today and are being hosted by League One outfit Burton Albion.
 You know how this works by now: team news, breathless updates from grounds where the drizzle is horizontal and frantic attempts to keep tabs on 48 different matches being played simultaneously across four different competitions. What could possibly go wrong?
